“Damn… it…………!”

I try to resist, but my body will not move.

I have no control of my limbs. Soon sensation itself will be stolen from me, fading until nothing remains.

“Damn…!”
I want to fight back, but my body will not move.
My limbs can’t move freely and my senses are being taken away, and I’m sure she will eliminate me.

“Farewell, my boy. If you must regret something, regret becoming a Master with power so pitiful.”

My body remains utterly still, helplessly accepting the touch of death.

My body does not move and accepts the finger of death.

“Any mage would be wary of a Caster whose art surpassed his own.

“…Were I your Master, I would grant a witch no freedom whatsoever. I would never permit you to summon a Servant who served as your limbs alone, rather than those of your Master.”

When a magus summons a familiar that is superior to him, I’m sure the relationship isn’t that of a servant and a master.
It is natural for the Master to be on his guard against a familiar of greater power.
…If I were your Master, I would not give any freedom to a witch. There is no way he would allow you to summon a Servant that would only obey your orders.”

pages.en:
But these are not beautiful in that fashion.

The will to destroy another.

The vanity that hungers to leave one’s name to posterity.

The rivalry that seeks to surpass the weapons fashioned by other hands.

The faith that drives one to accomplish some absolute feat.

Those impulses—the principles without which a celebrated or demonic blade can scarcely be created—are absent from these swords.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But they are not like that.
Fighting spirit that intends to beat others…
Desire to be famous…
Competitive spirit that tries to beat another weapon…
Faith to accomplish some great deed…
The sense of purpose found in famous swords and demonic swords is not in these.

pages.en:
…If I had to put it into words, their maker forged them simply because he wished to forge.

A matched pair of unadorned blades, created with an empty mind, as though the smith were questioning the very meaning of his own existence.

That is what they seem to be.

Swords like mirrors, without vanity.

Black and white, yin and yang—the awkward, honest work of a smith made steel.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…They were made because somebody wanted to make them.
Unrefined twin swords made without a will, as if to question the meaning of the swordsmith.
I think those are swords like that.
Mirrored swords without vanity.
Black and white, strange swords that represent yin and yang.

“What——”

The earth has been scorched red.

The magical energy compressed into each tiny light would fill the vessel of my body more than three times over.

Had one struck Archer directly, it would have torn away half his body. By now he would have shared the fate of the black shadow he cut down moments before.

Caster’s attack is an endless rain.

How are the descending bolts of light any different from a bombardment?

Each spell possesses power enough to kill in a single blow, yet Caster releases them one after another in a torrent.

As a mage, even I understand how far beyond all reason this magecraft lies.

Caster’s attack is a rain without pause.
The shooting lights are no different from a bombing raid.
Each magic is a deadly attack, and Caster is shooting them off like rain.
I may be an amateur, but even I can understand how ridiculous this ‘magic’ is.

Greater magecraft possesses tremendous power, and therefore demands time to cast.

Even a fully trained mage would require a minute for a spell of this magnitude. A practitioner of High-Speed Incantation would still need thirty seconds.

Even a magus that could use high-speed casting would take thirty seconds or so.

pages.en:
“I told you I would attempt only one blow.

“You evaded the first, so everything afterward was merely a courtesy. What is it? Did you wish me to break my word and strike you after all?”

The bastard delivers this outrageous answer with a perfectly straight face.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, I told you I’d try only once.
My first attack was avoided. Everything else was unnecessary. Or what? Did you want me to break my promise and hit you?”
He says such a ridiculous thing.

pages.ja:
「
。では、私を殺す気はなかったと？」
「つい挑発に乗っただけだ。私の目的はそこの男にあったからな。他のサーヴァントと戦うなど予定にはなかった」
pages.jaRuby:
「
。では、私を殺す気はなかったと？」
「つい挑発に乗っただけだ。私の目的はそこの男にあったからな。他のサーヴァントと戦うなど予定にはなかった」
pages.en:
“——. Then you never intended to kill me?”

“I merely allowed your provocation to carry me away. My purpose lay with the man standing there. Fighting another Servant was never part of my plans.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“. Then you had no intention of killing me?”
“I only responded to your provocation. My objective is that man over there. I didn’t intend to fight another Servant.”

pages.ja:
……む。
確かにあいつ、始めっからやる気がないというか、敵意らしき物を持っていなかったっけ。
pages.jaRuby:
……む。
確かにあいつ、始めっからやる気がないというか、敵意らしき物を持っていなかったっけ。
pages.en:
…Hm.

Come to think of it, from the beginning he seemed almost disinterested in the fight. I never sensed anything that could truly be called hostility.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Hm.
He certainly didn’t have any will to fight from the beginning…

pages.ja:
「……そう。どうやら私と戦いに来た、という訳ではなかったようねアーチャー」
「ああ、そこの男が腰抜けなのと同じでね。不必要な戦いは避けるのが主義だ。
剣を執る時は必勝の好機であり、必殺を誓った時のみだ。意味のない殺生は苦手でな」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…I see. Then you did not come here to fight me, Archer.”

“No. Like the coward standing there, I prefer to avoid unnecessary battle.

“I take up my swords only when victory is certain, and only when I have sworn to kill. Meaningless slaughter does not suit me.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. It does not look like you came here to fight me, Archer.”
“Nope. It’s just like that chicken over there. I try to avoid meaningless battles.
I only use my sword at perfect opportunities, and only when I can swear a sure kill. I don’t like killing meaninglessly.”

pages.ja:
……何がおかしいのか。
キャスターは口元を緩ませて、本当に愉快そうに微笑した。
pages.jaRuby:
……何がおかしいのか。
キャスターは口元を緩ませて、本当に愉快そうに微笑した。
pages.en: …For some reason, Caster’s lips soften into a smile of genuine delight.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…What’s so funny?
Caster laughs from the bottom of her heart.

pages.ja:
「そう。なら、アナタたちは似たもの同士という事？」
「「は？」」
声がはもる。
似たもの同士って、俺とアーチャーが？
その、一体どんな理由で？
pages.jaRuby:
「そう。なら、アナタたちは似たもの同士という事？」
「「は？」」
声がはもる。
似たもの同士って、俺とアーチャーが？
その、一体どんな理由で？
pages.en:
“I see. Then are the two of you perhaps alike?”

“What?”

Our voices overlap.

Alike? Archer and me?

By what conceivable reasoning?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Then you two are alike.”
““Huh?”“
We reply in unison.
Alike… Me and Archer?
What makes her say that?

pages.ja:
「違うのかしら。貴方たちは無益な殺生が嫌なのでしょう？ そこの坊やは私のような無関係な人間を糧にするサーヴァントが許せない。
貴方は無意味な殺戮は好まない。
ほら、まったく同じじゃない。だから手を組んでいるのではなくて？」
pages.jaRuby:
「違うのかしら。貴方たちは無益な殺生が嫌なのでしょう？ そこの坊やは私のような無関係な人間を糧にするサーヴァントが許せない。
貴方は無意味な殺戮は好まない。
ほら、まったく同じじゃない。だから手を組んでいるのではなくて？」
pages.en:
“Am I mistaken? You both abhor futile killing. The boy cannot forgive a Servant like me, who feeds upon innocent people.

“And you dislike slaughter without purpose.

“There. You are precisely alike. Is that not why you have joined forces?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Am I wrong? You both do not like meaningless killings, right? That boy over there cannot stand a Servant like me who feeds on innocent people.
You don’t like meaningless killings.
See, it’s exactly the same. Is that not why you two are cooperating?”

pages.ja: 「ばっ……！ どうしてそんなふざけた結論になる！ おまえ目が腐ってるぞ、誰がこんなヤツと一緒なもんか！」
pages.jaRuby: 「ばっ……！ どうしてそんなふざけた結論になる！ おまえ目が腐ってるぞ、誰がこんなヤツと一緒なもんか！」
pages.en: “What——!? How could you reach a conclusion that absurd!? Your eyes must be rotten! Who could possibly be anything like this bastard!?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “You idiot…! How can you reach that conclusion!? Who would ally with such a guy!”

pages.ja:
「
同感だ。平和主義者なのは同じだが、根本が大きく異なる。厄介事は早めに片づけるのが私の方針だ。
この男のように、いつまでも悩んだりはしない」
pages.jaRuby:
「
同感だ。平和主義者なのは同じだが、根本が大きく異なる。厄介事は早めに片づけるのが私の方針だ。
この男のように、いつまでも悩んだりはしない」
pages.en:
“I agree. We are both pacifists, but the resemblance ends there. My policy is to dispose of trouble before it matures.

“I do not agonize forever as this man does.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I feel the same way. We are both pacifists, but our principles are different. It is my principle to take care of problems early on.
I do not ponder forever like this man.”

pages.ja:
「っ、何が平和主義者だ！ 俺は忘れてないぞ。おまえはバーサーカーと一緒にセイバーを狙ったんだ。
セイバー一人に戦わせて、自分は安全なところにいたクセに……！」
pages.jaRuby:
「っ、何が平和主義者だ！ 俺は忘れてないぞ。おまえはバーサーカーと一緒にセイバーを狙ったんだ。
セイバー一人に戦わせて、自分は安全なところにいたクセに……！」
pages.en:
“What kind of pacifist are you!? I haven’t forgotten. You fired upon Saber along with Berserker.

“You made Saber fight alone while you watched from safety…!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What do you mean by pacifist!? I still remember. You shot at Saber along with Berserker.
Even though you were hiding in a safe place while Saber was fighting…!”

pages.ja:
「仕方なかろう。あの時はまだ共闘関係ではなかった。 セイバーの安全よりバーサーカーを倒す事が優先されただけだ。
それともなにか、目に映る物全てを助けろなどと言うのではあるまいな？ ならばバーサーカーとて倒す対象にはならないが」
「っ〜〜〜〜…………！」
pages.jaRuby:
「仕方なかろう。あの時はまだ共闘関係ではなかった。 セイバーの安全よりバーサーカーを倒す事が優先されただけだ。
それともなにか、目に映る物全てを助けろなどと言うのではあるまいな？ ならばバーサーカーとて倒す対象にはならないが」
「っ〜〜〜〜…………！」
pages.en:
“The circumstances demanded it. We were not allies at the time. Defeating Berserker simply took precedence over Saber’s safety.

“Or do you demand that I save everything before my eyes? By that reasoning, Berserker himself would cease to be a valid target.”

“Nghhh…………!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It couldn’t be helped. We were not cooperating back then. It’s just that defeating Berserker came before Saber’s safety.
Or what? Don’t tell me to save everyone I see. If that is the case, Berserker would have to be saved as well and I would not be able to fight him.”
“……!!”

pages.ja:
むーっ、と睨み合う。
ああもう、こいつとは本当に馬が合わない！
なんだってこう、こいつの台詞はことごとく癇に障りやがるのか……！
pages.jaRuby:

なんだってこう、こいつの台詞はことごとく癇に障りやがるのか……！
pages.en:
We glare furiously at each other.

Damn it all, I truly cannot get along with this man!

How does every word out of his mouth find precisely the right nerve to strike…!?
pages.mirrorMoon:
We glare at one another.
Man, I just can’t get along with him!
Why does everything he says get on my nerves…!?

……と。

pages.jaRuby:

」

そんな俺たちを見て、キャスターはますます楽しげに笑ってやがる。
pages.en:
“Heh.”

…And watching us, Caster’s amusement only deepens.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Fu”
…Then.
Caster laughs even more seeing us like this.

「？」
はあ、と首をかしげる。
アーチャーは俺から目を逸らし、一転して真剣にキャスターを睨み付けた。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I have taken a liking to you. Both your powers and the forms of your existence are rare.

“It would be a waste to make enemies of you.”

“?”

I tilt my head in confusion.

Archer looks away from me and, abruptly serious, fixes Caster with his gaze.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I like you two. Your powers and how you two exist are rare.
It would be disappointing to make you two my enemies.”
“?”
I tilt my head in wonder.
Archer looks away from me and glares at Caster.

pages.ja:
「……ちょっと待て。何が言いたいんだ、おまえ」
「判らない？ 私と手を組みなさい、と言っているのよ。
私なら今のパートナーより優れたモノを用意できるわ。
坊やにはセイバー以上のサーヴァントを。
貴方は今のマスターより優れた魔術師と契約できる」
pages.jaRuby:
「……ちょっと待て。何が言いたいんだ、おまえ」

坊やにはセイバー以上のサーヴァントを。
[ruby text=アーチャー char=2]貴方は今のマスターより優れた魔術師と契約できる」
pages.en:
“…Wait. What are you trying to say?”

“Do you not understand? I am proposing an alliance.

“I can provide each of you with a partner superior to the one you possess now.

“For the boy, a Servant greater than Saber.

“And for you, a contract with a mage greater than your present Master.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hold on. What do you want to say?”
“Can you not tell? I’m telling you to ally with me.
I can provide you two with better partners.
I can give you, boy, a Servant superior to Saber.
I can give you, Archer, a contract with a magus superior to your Master.”

pages.ja:
思考が停止する。
正直、この女が本気で言っているのか、その正気のほどを疑った。
pages.jaRuby:
思考が停止する。
正直、この女が本気で言っているのか、その正気のほどを疑った。
pages.en:
My thoughts come to a halt.

Truthfully, I cannot decide whether this woman is serious—or sane.
pages.mirrorMoon:
My mind freezes.
I question her sanity for asking such a question.

pages.ja:
「悪い話ではない筈よ。私にはこの戦いを終わらせる用意がある。言ったでしょう、勝つ事なんて容易いと。
どう？ 生き残りたいのなら、私に従うべきじゃなくて？」
pages.jaRuby:
「悪い話ではない筈よ。私にはこの戦いを終わらせる用意がある。言ったでしょう、勝つ事なんて容易いと。
どう？ 生き残りたいのなら、私に従うべきじゃなくて？」
pages.en:
“The offer is hardly unfavorable. I already possess the means to bring this war to an end. I told you, did I not? Victory itself will be easy.

“Well? If you wish to survive, should you not submit to me?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It can’t be a bad proposal. I told you two that I’m prepared to end this war, and winning is easy.
How about it? Should you not cooperate with me if you want to survive?”

pages.ja:

」

俺は無関係な人間を巻き込むヤツを止める為に戦うと決めた。
なら、こんなヤツには絶対に頷けない。

なら、こんなヤツには絶対に頷けない。
pages.en:
“————”

There is nothing to consider.

I resolved to fight in order to stop anyone who preyed upon innocent people.

I could never bow my head to someone like her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I don’t even need to think about it.
I decided to fight since I want to stop people like her who would involve innocent people.
So I can never accept her offer.

pages.ja:
「
断る。俺は、おまえみたいな魔女とは手を組まない」
断言する。

このサーヴァントとは手を組めないし、なにより俺たちは互いのパートナーを裏切らない。
俺はセイバーと共に戦っていくんだし、アーチャーだって、遠坂を裏切るような真似はしない。

「
断る。俺は、おまえみたいな魔女とは手を組まない」
断言する。
それは当然の答えだ。
このサーヴァントとは手を組めないし、なにより俺たちは互いのパートナーを裏切らない。
俺はセイバーと共に戦っていくんだし、アーチャーだって、遠坂を裏切るような真似はしない。
pages.en:
“I refuse. I will never ally myself with a witch like you.”

My answer is absolute.

Of course it is.

I cannot join forces with this Servant. More importantly, neither of us will betray our partner.

I will continue fighting beside Saber, and Archer would never betray Tohsaka either.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I refuse. I won’t ally with a witch like you.”
I declare so.
This is a natural response.
I can’t cooperate with this Servant, and more than anything, we won’t betray our partners.
I’ll be fighting with Saber, and Archer will not do anything to betray Tohsaka.

pages.jaRuby:

“————”

…Wait.

Why has that bastard been silent all this time?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
…Wait.
Why is he silent?

！」

pages.en:
“…Hey. Archer, you——!”

“I refuse. I have no reason to borrow your strength.

“More fundamentally, your faction lacks sufficient force. However far you expand your influence, you remain inferior to Berserker alone. The conditions are not yet favorable enough to join you.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Hey. Archer!”
“I refuse. There is no reason for me to need your power.
Before anything, your territory is too weak. No matter how strong it may be, it is still not stronger than Berserker. It is not a good enough condition to accept your offer.”

pages.en:

…I release the breath caught in my chest.

For a moment I had a terrible premonition, but he is not that sort of man.

I may dislike him, but his actions follow a logic he never betrays.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
…I sigh with relief.
I had a bad feeling, but he’s not like that.
I hate him, but he’s still firm on his beliefs.

pages.ja:
「そう。交渉は決裂、という事？」
「そうだ。だがここで君と戦う気はない。この場に居合わせたのは私の独断でね。マスターの命令ではないから君を討つ理由はない。ここは痛み分けという事で手を打たないか」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“I see. Then our negotiations have failed?”

“They have. But I have no intention of fighting you here. I came upon this place at my own discretion, not by my Master’s order. I therefore have no cause to destroy you. Shall we accept a draw and part ways?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. So there is no negotiation?”
“No. But I have no intention of fighting you here. It’s by my own choice that I’m here. It’s not my Master’s order, so there’s no reason for me to defeat you. How about we call this a draw?”

pages.ja:
「え
？」
その言動に、耳を疑った。
今、キャスターを見逃すと言ったのか……？
pages.jaRuby:
「え
？」
その言動に、耳を疑った。
今、キャスターを見逃すと言ったのか……？
pages.en:
“What?”

I cannot believe my ears.

Did he just offer to let Caster escape…?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Huh?”
I doubt my own ears.
Did he just say he’d let Caster go…?

pages.ja:
「……意外ね。アナタのマスターは私を追っていたでしょう？ なのにアナタは私を見逃すというの？」
「ああ。おまえがここで何人殺そうが知らん。それは私には与り知らぬ事だ」
pages.jaRuby:
「……意外ね。アナタのマスターは私を追っていたでしょう？ なのにアナタは私を見逃すというの？」
「ああ。おまえがここで何人殺そうが知らん。それは私には与り知らぬ事だ」
pages.en:
“…How unexpected. Your Master has been hunting me, has she not? Yet you intend to spare me?”

“I do. You may kill any number of people here. It is no concern of mine.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…That’s unexpected. Your Master was after me, right? But you’re saying you will let me go?”
“Yes. I don’t care how many people you kill here. It’s something I’ll ignore.”

pages.ja:
「
あら。ひどい男、毒は使いようということ？」
「私のマスターはマスター殺しに精力的でなくてね。
その分、おまえが他のマスターを潰してくれるのなら何かと助かる。この戦いの決着は、その後でも遅くはあるまい」
pages.jaRuby:
「
あら。ひどい男、毒は使いようということ？」
「私のマスターはマスター殺しに精力的でなくてね。
その分、おまえが他のマスターを潰してくれるのなら何かと助かる。この戦いの決着は、その後でも遅くはあるまい」
pages.en:
“My. What a cruel man. You believe even poison has its uses?”

“My Master is not especially enthusiastic about killing other Masters.

“If you eliminate them in her place, it will save us considerable trouble. We may settle matters between ourselves afterward.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh. How terrible of you. You think poison has its uses?”
“My Master isn’t that enthusiastic about killing other Masters.
So it’ll help me if you kill other Masters. We can settle our match after that.”

pages.ja: アーチャーの提案を受け入れたのか、キャスターは黒衣を翻す。
pages.jaRuby: アーチャーの提案を受け入れたのか、キャスターは黒衣を翻す。
pages.en: Perhaps accepting Archer’s proposal, Caster sweeps her black robes around herself.
pages.mirrorMoon: Caster must have accepted it as she turns around.

pages.ja:

消えようとするキャスターへと走り寄る。
が、それはアーチャーの手によって阻まれた。
pages.jaRuby:

消えようとするキャスターへと走り寄る。
が、それはアーチャーの手によって阻まれた。
pages.en:
“Wait, Caster…!”

I run toward her fading figure.

Archer’s hand bars my way.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hold on, Caster…!”
I run to Caster, who’s about to disappear.
But Archer stops me.

pages.ja:
「馬鹿か貴様。追えば確実に死ぬぞ」
冷淡な一言。
それは怒りで吐き気がするぐらい、真実味を帯びた言葉だった。
pages.jaRuby:
「馬鹿か貴様。追えば確実に死ぬぞ」
冷淡な一言。
それは怒りで吐き気がするぐらい、真実味を帯びた言葉だった。
pages.en:
“Are you a fool? Pursue her and you will certainly die.”
